task: Local worker-3 vmdk grew to 292G while the guest used 43G. Find the writer, cut its rewrite rate, record the lesson.

events.summary: Change only trivy-operator scannerReportTTL. Deliberately left alone: operator OOMKill, kubelet image GC, node disk shrink or rebuild, Harbor, other apps.

Guest used 43G vs host vmdk 292G; Prometheus 3d max guest usage ~47G on all nodes; node_disk_written 517GiB on worker-3 vs 53-128GiB elsewhere; top container_fs_writes writer is security-system scan-vulnerabilityreport pods.
scannerReportTTL 24h (chart default) to 168h so reports are not rescanned daily, each rescan re-downloading the Trivy DB to node disk.

events.scope: trivy-operator Application values and the static regression suite on the local Vagrant cluster. NOT covered: host vmdk reclaim (needs node rebuild, not approved), trivy-operator OOM and per-Job DB download (separate lane), Kakao cluster.
evidence: test:live local cluster: ConfigMap security-system/trivy-operator-config OPERATOR_SCANNER_REPORT_TTL=168h after push-to-gitea (confirmed by the author lane and independently by the PR #574 reviewer)

events.summary: In the repository and on the local cluster, trivy-operator scannerReportTTL is 168h, so VulnerabilityReports are refreshed weekly instead of daily and the daily re-download of the ~1 GB Trivy DB onto node disk stops. Host vmdk space already written is not reclaimed; that needs a node rebuild and is out of scope.
Complete for the rewrite-rate prevention scope of this PR within repository and local-cluster scope; host reclaim (owner decision) and the per-Job DB download / operator OOM are tracked separately.
